h1:
🏅 Best Michelin restaurants in Surat Thani
Island and mainland on one list
intro: What makes Surat Thani fun is that its Michelin picks straddle both the mainland town and Ko Samui. On the island, Baan Suan Lung Khai and Jun Hom plate up southern Thai cooking and seafood pulled straight from the water, while in town Dear Phangan and the beloved Keo Pla fish-dumpling noodles keep locals queuing.
quickAnswerHtml: Surat Thani has 9 Michelin restaurants for 2026, all Bib Gourmand, with no starred spots.

blocks.html: What makes Surat Thani fun is that its Michelin picks straddle both the mainland town and Ko Samui. On the island, Baan Suan Lung Khai and Jun Hom plate up southern Thai cooking and seafood pulled straight from the water, while in town Dear Phangan and the beloved Keo Pla fish-dumpling noodles keep locals queuing.

blocks.name: Baan Suan Lung Khai
blocks.descHtml:
Baan Suan Lung Khai sits on Round-Island Road Route 4170 in Ban Taling Ngam, on the south side of Koh Samui, about a 40-minute drive from Chaweng Beach and close to the Virgin Coast side and the island's sunset viewpoints. The restaurant is open every day in two seatings, 11:00–14:00 and 16:30–19:30, but only for guests who have booked ahead — walk-ins are not accepted at all, since Lung Khai prepares ingredients based on each day's reservation count. You need to call at least 1 day ahead at 098-015-2845 or 083-984-5629 (Wongnai notes LINE booking is also available). During high season, Dec–Feb, book several days ahead.

Pricing is a set menu per person, with 4 price tiers to choose from: 350, 500, 700, or 1,000 baht. When you book, let them know your headcount and budget, and the kitchen will put together a meal based on that day's fresh ingredients. Dress is casual, since you're eating out in a coconut grove. The recommended time is the evening seating at 16:30, so you finish in time to head to the sunset viewpoint on the Taling Ngam side right after. The daytime seating suits anyone staying on the south side or doing an island driving loop. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Southern seafood set — picked blue swimmer crab and grilled prawns, served on a woven tray under a dome cover
mustOrder: Southern seafood set (picked blue swimmer crab, grilled prawns)
Pandan coconut rice on a woven tray under a dome cover
Traditional local sweets to close the set
blocks.bestFor: Anyone who wants Southern Thai seafood from local fishermen in a coconut grove on Samui's south side, ready to book ahead
blocks.libCredit: Photo: Baan Suan Lung Khai official Facebook page

blocks.name: Dear Phangan
blocks.descHtml:
Budget runs around THB 800–1,000 per person for a chef's blind tasting menu that changes daily based on ingredients. The most important thing to know: the restaurant only opens for sittings with advance bookings, with no fixed operating hours, and it does not accept walk-ins because the kitchen cooks strictly to the number of guests booked. Book by calling 089-114-3302 or messaging the restaurant's Facebook page (dearphangan). During the island's high season, book several days ahead, since the chef only takes a limited number of guests per day based on available ingredients.

The restaurant sits in the Hin Kong–Wok Tum area on the west side of Koh Phangan — you can use Koh Phangan Hospital as your landmark, since the restaurant is right nearby, on the same plot of land as the Baan Nui homestay. From Thong Sala pier, it's not far by motorbike or hired songthaew heading to the west side. Dress is casual, and it's worth booking an evening sitting so you can catch the sunset at Hin Kong beach beforehand. When you call to book, let them know your headcount along with any allergies or dishes to avoid, so the chef can plan ingredients accordingly. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Crispy fermented catfish, crisp outside and moist inside
mustOrder: Crispy fermented catfish (the dish MICHELIN praised)
Fresh squid dishes from the Phangan pier
Blind tasting menu based on the day's ingredients — let the chef decide
blocks.bestFor: Couples and groups of friends staying on the west side of Koh Phangan who want a one-of-a-kind home-cooked special meal, without worrying about advance booking
blocks.hours: Open only for sittings with advance bookings; no fixed operating hours
blocks.libCredit: Photo: Dear Phangan official Facebook page

blocks.name: Jun Hom
blocks.descHtml:
Jun Hom sits on Mae Nam–Bang Po beach, on the north side of Koh Samui, Surat Thani province. Budget runs around 250–500 THB per person, and the plates come large enough to share, so the more people you bring the better the value. Open every day — Wongnai lists 10:00–22:00, while the Koh Samui municipal website lists 11:00–21:00 — so if you're planning an early or late visit, it's worth calling ahead to check at 077-236-458 or 077-602-008. The restaurant is mainly walk-in, but MICHELIN notes the restaurant handles bookings itself by phone, which is worth using if you're going in the evening, since it's open-air right on the beach with limited tables and a kitchen that cooks one dish at a time — tables fill up around sunset, so budget extra time for your food to arrive.

Getting there means driving a car or rented motorbike along the ring road on the island's north side; the Mae Nam/Bang Po zone sits along the route from Na Thon pier toward Bo Phut beach, with no regular public transport. The best time to go is late afternoon before 5pm, to grab a seaside table before the crowds arrive, or a relaxed lunch when tables are easy to find. Dress is casual — there's no dress code. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Fried lek khon fish, a local Samui fish hard to find off the island
mustOrder: Fried lek khon fish (local Samui fish)
blocks.bestFor: A big shared seafood meal by the sea with friends or family, best at sunset on Samui's north side
blocks.libCredit: Photo: Jun Hom Seafood Koh Samui official Facebook page

blocks.name: Keo Pla
blocks.descHtml:
Keo Pla is one of the easiest and cheapest restaurants to visit on Surat Thani's MICHELIN list, with bowls under THB 100. Open daily 08:00-14:30, but don't count on the closing time — dishes tend to sell out before then, especially the fish wontons and celery-stuffed fish rolls, which usually run out by around 11:30. Customers pack in from mid-morning, so the safest bet is to go for breakfast or an early lunch, before noon at the latest. It's walk-in only with no advance booking, but you can call 077-282-022 to check if it's open as usual that day.

The shop is on Na Mueang Road, right in downtown Surat Thani (Talat sub-district) — the easiest landmark is that it sits across from Colisseum Department Store, just a few minutes away by car or motorbike taxi from anywhere in town. If you're catching a morning boat to Koh Samui or Koh Phangan, stopping in for breakfast beforehand is a perfect fit. Order the fish wontons, fish roll, and fish balls together in one bowl for the best value. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Fish wontons made fresh daily + celery-stuffed fish rolls
blocks.bestFor: A budget breakfast-lunch in downtown Surat Thani before catching the boat to Samui/Phangan

blocks.name: Lucky
mustOrder: Sour curry with coconut shoot and sea bass
blocks.bestFor: A family meal or a meal for guests in downtown Surat Thani, or a Southern Thai meal before the boat to Samui-Phangan

blocks.name: Pa Ting (Don Sak)
blocks.descHtml:
A very comfortable budget for a MICHELIN-listed restaurant, running around 250–500 THB per person, and it takes credit cards too. It's walk-in, no reservation needed, but if you want to check ahead or you're coming as a large group, you can call 063-982-6959 (the number listed in the MICHELIN Guide) or 077-371-126 and 092-956-5593. Hours are Monday 9:00–20:30 and Tuesday–Sunday 9:30–20:30, with the restaurant's Facebook page noting last order at 20:30. Dress is casual.

The restaurant sits by the water at Pak Khlong Don Sak, Don Sak district, Surat Thani, around 10 minutes by car from the ferry pier to Koh Samui/Koh Pha Ngan. That's exactly the planning tip — if you're heading to Samui by car and ferry, build in time to stop for lunch or dinner right before boarding. Or if you're on your way back from the islands, it's perfectly placed for a stop before the long drive into town. The busiest times are around ferry departure and arrival slots, so if you want to sit back and enjoy the water without fighting for a table, aim to come a bit before or after those times. Dishes that should be on your table: crab and cha khram curry, salted grey mullet spicy salad, and boiled white clams with lemongrass. Read the full review →

blocks.bestFor: Stop for real Southern-style seafood before or after the ferry to Koh Samui-Pha Ngan — a light-budget family meal by the water

blocks.signature: Natural river prawns from the Tapi River
mustOrder: River prawns from the Tapi River
blocks.bestFor: Stop for southern Thai food with Tapi River prawns and mountain views, before/after your flight or train connection in Phunphin, or on the way to Samui or Cheow Lan

blocks.name: Yok Kheng
blocks.descHtml:
Yok Kheng sits on Ton Pho Road, in the old market area right in the middle of Surat Thani, near Coliseum Surat Thani. It's easy to find if you start from the mall and walk into the old market area. Prices are very easy on the wallet — noodles run about 50-80 baht a bowl, and a budget of around a hundred baht per person covers both a bowl of long tong and dessert. It's walk-in only, no reservations needed, and cash only, so remember to bring bills.

One thing to watch out for is the hours, since sources don't agree — several sources list daily 10:00-22:00, but Wongnai lists 11:30-16:30. The safe move is to call ahead before you head over, at 077-282-285 or 081-893-8918, especially if you're planning to go in the evening. The safest bet is lunchtime, when every source agrees the shop is open. If you're heading on to Koh Samui, Koh Phangan, or Khao Sok, stopping here for a bowl of long tong before you board a boat or a bus fits perfectly into the trip, since the shop sits right in town, which is already the province's main transit hub. faq.q: How many Michelin restaurants does Surat Thani have?
faq.a: For 2026 there are 9, all Bib Gourmand with no starred restaurants yet. They split between the mainland town and Ko Samui.

faq.q: Which one should I book ahead?
faq.a: On Samui, aim for Baan Suan Lung Khai and Jun Hom. Both do southern Thai and seafood and fill up fast in high season, so a call ahead saves you a wait.

faq.q: Where do I start if I want to eat cheap?
faq.a: Go for Yok Kheng, a noodle spot around 50 to 80 baht, or Keo Pla fish-dumpling noodles at roughly 100 baht a bowl. Both are easy, honest local plates in town.

faq.q: Are there Michelin restaurants on Ko Samui itself?
faq.a: Yes. Baan Suan Lung Khai and Jun Hom are both on Samui, leaning into southern Thai and seafood, easy to slot into an island day. The rest sit mostly in Surat Thani town.

faq.q: What is worth trying in the mainland town?
faq.a: Dear Phangan serves Thai, while Nampetch and Phunisa lean southern. For noodles there's Keo Pla and Yok Kheng, all walkable in town without crossing to the island.
